blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Discrete image generators learn the distribution of tokens produced by an image tokenizer. These token representations should be easy for generators to model, not merely enable faithful image reconstruction. Yet these tokenizers are commonly trained to reconstruct pixels, which prioritizes low-level fidelity and may disrupt representation structure useful for generation. Motivated by feature-predictive self-supervised learning, we introduce feature-loss tokenization (FeaTok), which trains discrete tokens by reconstructing pretrained features rather than pixels. Ablations across SigLIP, SigLIP2, DINOv2, and DINOv3 show better generative performance with FeaTok. In class-conditional generation, FeaTok advances the quality-compute Pareto frontier, reducing gFDr6 at 256x256 by up to 29 percent over the strongest discrete baselines and outperforming the strongest unguided continuous baseline (RAEv2) with 38 times less sampling compute. FeaTok also achieves higher human-preference reward-model scores than prior art without reward-based training and surpasses continuous and discrete text-conditional baselines on three benchmarks with only 500 fine-tuning updates after pre-training.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Image generation enables machines to create new visual content, supporting applications ranging from creative design to multimodal interaction.
A growing body of work represents images as discrete tokens and models them autoregressively ( Sun et al., 2024 ; Tian et al., 2024 ; Yu et al., 2026 ) .
Discrete tokens share the interface of language models, which makes them a natural choice for unified multimodal models.
They also sample an image with an order of magnitude less compute than continuous diffusion models, as shown in Fig. 1 .

blocks.en:
Image generation quality depends on discrete tokens that are both expressive and easy for a generator to model.
Previous discrete tokenizers focus on reconstruction performance, which targets the first property, expressivity .
However, generation also depends on the second property, which we call generative learnability : how easily a generator fits the token distribution at a given budget.
These two properties do not always align, as observed for both continuous and discrete image tokenizers and generators ( Gu et al., 2024 ; Yao et al., 2025 ; Ramanujan et al., 2025 ) .

blocks.en:
Generative learnability is related to the structure of a representation ( Skorokhodov et al., 2025 ; Chu et al., 2026 ) ,
which is in turn induced by the training target.
Pixel reconstruction prioritizes high-variance image details over
features useful for perception ( Balestriero and Lecun, 2024 ) , and
using self-supervised learning (SSL) objectives to predict features instead of pixels yields more semantically meaningful representations ( Assran et al., 2023 ) .
We refer to the representations of encoders trained with SSL objectives in feature space
as pretrained visual features (see Def. 1 ). Moreover, RAE ( Zheng et al., 2026b ) and RAEv2 ( Singh et al., 2026 ) show that the benefits of pretrained visual features go beyond representation learning and successfully transfer to image generation.

blocks.en:
Wang et al. (2024) trained discrete tokens by reconstructing the features of
image-understanding encoders instead of pixels, and showed that these tokens can outperform
pixel-trained VQ tokens for image generation.
Yet the discrete tokenizers that followed still use pixel reconstruction as the central loss,
and add pretrained visual features with additional losses ( Xiong et al., 2025 ; Du et al., 2026 ; Yu et al., 2026 ; Zheng et al., 2026a ; Chen et al., 2026b ) .
This raises the question of whether pixel reconstruction loss is essential for modern discrete tokenizer training used for downstream image generation .
We argue that it is not.
Feature objectives should shape both the encoder, pretrained in feature space,
and the discrete tokens.

blocks.en:
We introduce feature-loss tokenization ( FeaTok ), which separates discrete
representation learning from image reconstruction.
Instead of a pixel decoder and a pixel reconstruction loss, a feature decoder that reconstructs
pretrained visual features shapes the discrete tokens.
A separate image decoder is trained with pixel losses on detached tokens and only renders generated token sequences, so pixel losses never shape the discrete representation.
We additionally discretize the encoder’s global representation ( e.g. , CLS token), and generate it before the patch tokens, giving them image-level context. We call this global-augmented generative modelling.
Ablations in Sec. 2.2 show that FeaTok has better spatial structure and
generates better than tokenizers trained with pixel or combined losses for all four encoders we
study, and that global-augmented modelling contributes to this improvement.

blocks.en:
In this section, we present FeaTok , which learns discrete tokens by reconstructing pretrained visual features.
We use this term to distinguish representations by their pretraining objective.

我们使用这一术语来区分陈述的预先训练目标。

blocks.en:
We define pretrained visual features as representations of encoders learned by self-supervision in feature space,
including language–image contrastive learning ( Radford et al., 2021 ; Zhai et al., 2023 ; Tschannen et al., 2025 ) and self-distillation ( Caron et al., 2021 ; Oquab et al., 2024 ; Siméoni et al., 2026 ; Tschannen et al., 2025 ) .
Encoders trained by pixel reconstruction ( He et al., 2022 ) are excluded.

blocks.en:
Leveraging global tokens. In addition to patch features, various vision encoders supply a global representation, e.g. , a CLS token in DINO ( Caron et al., 2021 ; Oquab et al., 2024 ; Siméoni et al., 2026 ) or a global pooling token in SigLIP ( Zhai et al., 2023 ; Tschannen et al., 2025 ) .
Replacing pixel reconstruction with feature reconstruction losses
naturally suggests discretizing this global feature along
with patches.
The benefit of doing so is that it allows us to define a hierarchical generative model
that first generates the global token and then the patch tokens conditioned on it
which simplifies the conditional distributions of the patch tokens by providing a global context.
This global representation is generally ignored by discrete tokenizers
trained using pixel-reconstruction losses,
as the pixel reconstruction over patches does not provide direct supervision on the
global feature discretization.
Prior work follows a similar global-to-local strategy, using learned holistic
tokens ( Zheng et al., 2025a ) , coarse-to-fine token sequences ( Bachmann et al., 2025 ) ,
or separately generated semantic codes ( Lavoie et al., 2025 ) .
In our case, the global token directly discretizes the pretrained encoder’s global representation.

Fréchet distance in the Inception space can misrank modern generative models, and

judgments ( Stein et al., 2023 ) .

In App. F we report gFID ( Heusel et al., 2017 ) and precision, recall ( Kynkäänniemi et al., 2019 ) ,
density and coverage ( Naeem et al., 2020 ) in Inception space as complementary diagnostics.

All four FeaTok-L variants outperform the strongest prior discrete baseline in gFDr6, showing consistent gains across four pretrained visual feature encoders satisfying Def. 1 .

blocks.en: 4 Related work
blocks.zh: 4 相关工作

blocks.en:
Pretrained representations for continuous generation. Continuous generators show that the pretraining objective of the features matters.
RAE ( Zheng et al., 2026b ) and RAEv2 ( Singh et al., 2026 ) train diffusion models in the feature
spaces of pretrained vision encoders, paired with learned image decoders, and RAE finds that MAE
features ( He et al., 2022 ) reconstruct best but generate worse than DINOv2 features.
REPA ( Yu et al., 2025b ) aligns intermediate SiT ( Ma et al., 2024 ) features with pretrained
representations, where MAE is the weakest of the tested targets, and DDT ( Wang et al., 2026 ) adopts this alignment.
REG ( Wu et al., 2025 ) denoises a pretrained class token together with the image latents,
VA-VAE ( Yao et al., 2025 ) aligns VAE latents with a pretrained vision encoder, and
REPA-E ( Leng et al., 2025 ) tunes the VAE and the diffusion model end to end with the REPA loss.

blocks.en:
Discrete tokenization with pretrained representations. VQ-VAE ( Van Den Oord et al., 2017 ) learns discrete image tokens through pixel reconstruction, and later
tokenizers simplify the quantizer ( Yu et al., 2024a ; Mentzer et al., 2024 ) . Wang et al. (2024) train tokenizers to reconstruct the features
from image understanding encoders, and in autoregressive generation
all but the MAE teacher outperform pixel-trained VQGAN tokens.
Recent tokenizers keep pixel reconstruction as the central objective and add pretrained encoder
features through feature alignment ( Yu et al., 2026 ) , semantic regularization ( Xiong et al., 2025 ) ,
self-distillation ( Du et al., 2026 ) , or feature reconstruction from several encoder
depths ( Jia et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2026b ; Zheng et al., 2025b ; Zheng et al., 2026a ) .
TA-Tok ( Han et al., 2025 ) trains feature-reconstructed tokens for unified multimodal models, but decodes
images through pixel-trained VQ tokens or latents.
In FeaTok, only pretrained visual features (Def. 1 ) shape the tokens, which
reconstruct a multi-layer target and include a quantized global token.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented FeaTok, a discrete image tokenizer whose tokens are shaped only by feature
reconstruction, while a pixel decoder trained on detached tokens renders them into images.
We also discretize the encoder’s global representation and model it together with the patch tokens.
Across four pretrained encoders, FeaTok generates better than tokenizers trained with pixel
or combined losses.
FeaTok achieves the best gFDr6 among the evaluated discrete generators on ImageNet at × 256 256\!\times\!256 and × 512 512\!\times\!512 , outperforms continuous generators at a matched sampling cost, achieves higher
human-preference reward-model scores, and transfers to text-to-image generation after pretraining
and only 500 500 fine-tuning updates.
We believe these results are a step toward effective discrete representations for unified
multimodal modeling, and that the low sampling cost of FeaTok makes it attractive for scaling
multimodal training.

blocks.en:
BAR generative model. Recall that BAR learns tokens with FSQ in a bit representation and models their distribution
with an adapted autoregressive model.
Instead of a single categorical prediction over the entire codebook, BAR uses a
lightweight masked bit modeling head.
During training, some bits of the target token are masked, and the head learns
to recover them with a bit-wise cross-entropy objective.
During sampling, it starts with all bits masked and progressively fills them in,
conditioning later predictions on the bits already revealed.
The autoregressive context stays fixed during these within-token steps.
Once the token is complete, it becomes part of the context for the next token.
This avoids an output distribution with one logit per codebook entry while
allowing dependencies among a token’s bits.

blocks.en:
Pixel fidelity versus perceptual quality. Feature supervision lowers PSNR and SSIM for all four encoders, e.g. , from 20.61 20.61 to 17.45 17.45 PSNR for DINOv3, so the tokens no longer reproduce each input pixel by pixel.
For image generation, however, the goal is images that look real to humans, not pixel-exact
copies of a given input.
PSNR and SSIM compare each reconstruction with its input pixel by pixel, so they penalize small
shifts of texture and detail that humans barely notice, and they correlate poorly with human
perceptual judgments ( Zhang et al., 2018 ) .
Distribution-level metrics instead ask whether the images look like real images, and they favor
feature supervision.
Feature targets improve rFDr6 for three of the four encoders, and the same feature-supervised
tokenizers give lower gFID in the controlled ablations (Tab. 11 ),
the best gFDr6 among discrete generators (Tab. 1 ), and higher human-preference
reward-model scores (Fig. 5 ).
The lower paired pixel fidelity is therefore a trade-off rather than a free improvement.
Feature-supervised tokens discard some input detail, and not all of it need be perceptually
irrelevant, but for generation the trade-off favors feature supervision in the distribution-level
and reward-model evaluations above.

blocks.en:
gFID measures the Fréchet distance in the feature space of an Inception-v3
network ( Szegedy et al., 2016 ) trained for ImageNet classification.
Its sensitivity to ImageNet class information means that it can be lowered substantially without
improving the images ( Kynkäänniemi et al., 2023 ) , and Inception features represent the content
of modern generators poorly, so gFID often disagrees with human raters ( Stein et al., 2023 ; Jayasumana et al., 2024 ) .
These problems are most severe at the low values reached by current ImageNet generators.
ImageNet validation images score a gFID of 1.68 1.68 against the training set ( Yang et al., 2026 ) , so
generators below 2.0 2.0 , and especially below 1.68 1.68 , appear as close to the training data as real
images, although their samples remain clearly distinguishable from real ones ( Yang et al., 2026 ) .
In this regime, gFID can also be optimized directly: post-training a generator on Inception features
lowers its gFID from 3.31 3.31 to 0.81 0.81 without producing the best samples, whereas post-training on
modern representations improves object structure while gFID becomes worse ( Yang et al., 2026 ) .
gFDr6 addresses these issues by averaging Fréchet distances over six representation spaces,
each normalized by the distance between the training and validation sets, so no single feature
space dominates and a value of 1 1 means as close to the training data as real validation images.
